title: Distributed transactions and two-phase commit

kcs.statement: In two-phase commit a coordinator first asks every participant to prepare (each votes yes only after durably recording its changes and holding locks), then sends commit if all voted yes and abort otherwise.
Two-phase commit is blocking: if the coordinator fails after participants voted yes, they keep holding locks and cannot decide on their own until it recovers.
Two-phase commit gives atomicity across stores at the cost of latency and availability, so it suits a few tightly coupled databases, not long-running business flows across services.
